subject: Request: Exec approval for 30% Hosted API concession - HealthWorks AI (HW-2026-07)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Exec approval for 30% Hosted API concession - HealthWorks AI (HW-2026-07)

Ben —

Quick context: HealthWorks AI (lead Dr. Serena Patel) is asking for a 30% Hosted API unit-rate concession vs our standard published retail for a 12-month initial term. They are promising a committed ramp: $1.2M committed consumption within 12 months (monthly ramp schedule attached). They require US data residency and a dedicated capacity lane for predictable latency. Key asks from the customer: 30% off per-token usage rate, a 12-month minimum term, and a repricing trigger at renewal if usage materially undershoots.

Why this matters: this is a strategic anchor for the healthcare vertical (their pilot includes three enterprise customers and an integration partner). If we win this at proposed economics, we expect a >2x reference pipeline in 9–12 months. Without concession they are likely to pilot with a competitor.

What I need from you: exec signoff for a 30% concession (one-time manager/deal-desk signoff route would be slower; they need a yes by EOD to keep their procurement timeline). If you want conditions, I can accept a 30% for 12 months conditioned on: (1) $900k minimum committed spend within 12 months, (2) 30-day prepay or 60-day invoice terms, (3) legal signoff on the data residency and SLA clause.

Attachments: price_proposal_v3.xlsx (detailed unit economics), security_and_soc2_packet.pdf (customer-facing).

Thanks — I appreciate a quick call if you want to talk through tradeoffs.

— Irene
Account Executive, Healthcare Vertical
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec approval for 30% Hosted API concession - HealthWorks AI (HW-2026-07)

Ben / Marcus —

Thanks for the context, Irene — forwarding my deal-desk read. Quoting Irene's summary below for thread continuity.

On Fri, 9 Oct 2026 at 09:12 Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben —
> 
> Quick context: HealthWorks AI (lead Dr. Serena Patel) is asking for a 30% Hosted API unit-rate concession vs our standard published retail for a 12-month initial term...

Deal-desk recommendation (initial):
- Baseline approval band for strategic pilots: up to 20% (deal desk). Anything over 20% requires exec signoff.
- Given the $1.2M committed ask and the strategic vertical value, recommend a structured concession: 20% for the first 90 days (pilot), then step to 30% once $300k consumption achieved OR on month 4 onward, whichever comes first. Alternatively, we can approve a straight 25% across 12 months to reduce margin exposure.

Financials (quick):
- Published blended rate: $0.0025 per token (example).
- 30% concession -> $0.00175 per token. Year-1 impact (est): -$320k gross margin vs list assuming the committed $1.2M at baseline consumption profile.

Operational asks: dedicated capacity lane is feasible (we'll need a labeled capacity pool), legal to approve data-residency wording, Finance to accept either prepay or 60-day net. Also need HubSpot deal updated with revised ACV and concession memo.

Requested decision: Exec authorization for >20% (target 30%) OR approval for our structured step approach (20% -> 30%).

Irene — attaching a short concession memo and a P&L delta table.

— Karthik
Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: deal_desk_concession_memo.pdf]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec approval for 30% Hosted API concession - HealthWorks AI (HW-2026-07)

Ben —

I reviewed the numbers and the strategic justification. My recommendation: approve the 30% concession for a 12-month term with the following binding conditions to protect revenue and enable Finance: 
1) Customer signs the revised MSA with Section 6.3 (prepay/commit clause) and a minimum committed spend of $900,000 within 12 months (failure to meet the threshold triggers automatic reprice to standard list for remaining term).
2) We include a mid-term usage review at month 6 with the option to reset pricing if actuals < 60% of committed ramp.
3) Customer agrees to quarterly business reviews and a public case study permission (marketing) after pilot completion.
4) Legal to approve the exact data-residency + dedicated-lane language; the concession is contingent on no open legal risk.

If you approve, I will: (a) create a formal concession memo, (b) update HubSpot and route paper to Finance for billing plan (prepay vs net-60), and (c) flag the capacity team to reserve the dedicated lane.

From a P&L perspective the worst-case margin hit is manageable given downstream reference and partner introductions. I support approval on the conditions above.

— Marcus
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: financial_delta_table.csv]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec approval for 30% Hosted API concession - HealthWorks AI (HW-2026-07)

Team —

Approved. Exec authorization granted for a 30% Hosted API concession for HealthWorks AI under the conditions Marcus outlined. Summarizing the approval terms to make it explicit: 
- Concession: 30% off Hosted API usage rates for an initial 12-month contractual period.
- Minimum committed spend: $900,000 within 12 months (must be in the signed contract).
- Billing: prefer 30-day prepay; Finance will accept net-60 only if Procurement agrees and Legal confirms credit protections.
- Repricing: if customer fails to meet the committed threshold, automatic reprice to standard list for the remainder of the term.
- Operational: dedicated capacity lane to be reserved on confirmation of signed MSA; Capacity & Engineering to be looped by Marcus.
- Documentation: Deal Desk to produce a concession memo and attach to the HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876543). DocuSign MSA link to be included in the deal record.

Irene — please coordinate with Serena to get signatures and confirm the procurement timeline. Marcus / Karthik — please file the concession memo and update billing. Legal: please prioritize review of the data-residency and SLA language.

Ben Carter
SVP, Sales — Redwood Inference
[Signed]
